claims.statement: Profiles.json is the single source of truth for Pulsar configuration; ConfigService resolves its path once in the constructor, defaulting to %AppData%\Pulsar\Profiles.json with an injectable configPath override (used by tests and ui-debug mode to redirect away from the production profile), and exposes it as ConfigFilePath so consumers never recompute the path.

The ProfilesConfig root model has four top-level regions: Settings (ProfileSettings with global app, gesture, hotkey, logging, and onboarding/tutorial state), Plugins (Dictionary<string, PluginProfile> keyed by PluginId, holding Enabled, a free-form Config store, and GrantedPermissions), Profiles (Dictionary<string, ProcessProfile> with CommandMode/SwitchMode PluginSlot lists), and InstalledPresetPacks (preset-pack install state with slot provenance for precise uninstall); absent InstalledPresetPacks loads as an empty list so old configs remain compatible.

Profiles and Plugins dictionaries are case-insensitive (StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase); because System.Text.Json deserializes dictionaries as case-sensitive by default, ConfigService and ConfigBackupService rebuild them with the comparer after every load so lookups like Profiles["Global"] and Profiles["global"] resolve identically.

PluginProfile.Config is Dictionary<string, object>, and JSON round-trips materialize values as JsonElement; both the load path and the SaveAsync path run NormalizeConfigDictionary to convert JsonElement values to concrete types (string, int/long/double, bool; arrays and objects become JSON strings), so type-consistent values reach validation and disk.

GetSnapshot() returns a JSON round-trip deep copy taken under the cache lock, so mutating the result can never affect the shared cache; the read-only snapshot contract is enforced by behavior rather than caller discipline (ADR-009), and CloneConfig rebuilds the case-insensitive Profiles dictionary so snapshot readers see live-cache lookup semantics.

LoadSnapshotAsync(forceReload: false) returns the live cached object by reference; only GetSnapshot() deep-copies, so callers that receive the LoadSnapshotAsync result must not mutate it — the documented division is read via snapshots, write via ConfigEditSession.

Every persisted change flows through ConfigEditSession; the plugin runtime is explicitly read-only — PluginRuntimeKernel.ApplyProfileAsync applies the user's persisted plugin profile (or defaults) but never writes back to Profiles.json, so activating a plugin cannot pollute the single source of truth (ADR-009).

ConfigEditSession.BeginAsync loads a snapshot and deep-clones it twice — an editable Draft and a _base baseline for detecting untouched regions — and captures store.CurrentRevision as the commit guard; CommitAsync saves Draft with that expected revision and re-arms to the store's new revision after success so a long-lived editor (e.g. the Settings window) can save repeatedly.

On a ConfigConcurrencyException, ConfigEditSession rebases exactly once: it reloads the current snapshot and folds concurrent writers' changes into untouched regions (Settings, InstalledPresetPacks, and each Profiles/Plugins entry that still equals the session baseline or is absent from the draft), keeping the user's edited regions, then re-arms the revision and retries the commit.

ConfigEditSession.RunAsync begins a session, applies a mutation, and skips the commit when the draft is JSON-equal to the baseline, so ensure-style operations never produce redundant writes or revision bumps; it commits once otherwise.

ConfigService.SaveAsync is a single-writer operation guarded by a SemaphoreSlim(1,1); the optimistic-concurrency check (expectedRevision vs CurrentRevision) runs inside the write lock so check and revision bump are atomic — two sessions started from the same revision can never both commit — and a mismatch throws ConfigConcurrencyException instead of silently overwriting a newer writer.

Saves are crash-safe: ConfigService writes a unique temp file (Profiles.json.<guid>.tmp), replaces the target with File.Move(..., overwrite: true), retries up to 3 times with 100 ms delay on IOException, cleans up leftover temp files best-effort, and copies the new file to Profiles.json.bak after each successful save (a failed backup never fails the save).

ConfigUpdated is raised outside the write lock after the cache update and revision bump, so subscribers (e.g. HotkeyService) may synchronously trigger another SaveAsync without deadlocking (ADR-005); the in-memory cache is replaced and CurrentRevision incremented under _cacheLock.

CurrentRevision is a monotonic long bumped on every successful save; ResetToFirstLaunchAsync also increments it (invalidating any in-flight ConfigEditSession whose revision no longer matches a surviving config) after clearing the cache and deleting Profiles.json plus its rolling .bak so the pre-reset config cannot be resurrected on the next launch.

A missing Profiles.json is never treated as a factory reset: unless the load is an explicit reset reload, ConfigService first restores the rolling Profiles.json.bak and only a genuine first launch (no file, no backup) generates and persists the default fallback config (light theme, Global profile with Notepad/Explorer/Calculator switch slots and a Command Prompt command slot, onboarding NotStarted).

Load-time reads capture the revision before opening the file and only replace the cached config if the revision is unchanged, so a concurrent successful save invalidates a stale disk read instead of letting old data overwrite the newer cache; load also normalizes dictionaries, JsonElement values, missing slot actions (from plugin metadata), and relative winSwitcher switch launch paths (resolved to absolute and persisted once so the file heals on disk).

If the config file parse fails, ConfigService preserves the last successfully loaded cache in memory and never overwrites the on-disk file with a fallback; only when no cache exists does it create an in-memory fallback without saving, and the _loadFailed flag makes smart detection skip persisting to avoid clobbering the valid file.

ConfigValidationPipeline runs five validation stages in order — plugin schema validation, plugin custom IPluginConfigurable.ValidateSettings, slot argument validation against action parameter metadata (required/type/validators with alias fallbacks), plugin dependency checks, and duplicate-hotkey warnings — producing a ValidationResult of errors, warnings, and infos.

Validation blocks persistence: SaveAsync throws InvalidOperationException when the pipeline reports errors, while warnings are logged and the save proceeds; an exception thrown by the pipeline itself is logged and does not block the save. On load, validation failures are logged but never block loading.

The validation pipeline is injected into the concrete ConfigService only after startup by AppStartupCoordinator.ConfigureValidationPipeline (after plugin discovery), because ConfigService is constructed before the plugin registry exists.

ConfigBackupService exports and imports the full configuration as a versioned ZIP (format version 1) containing manifest.json (format version, app version, creation time, ContainsSecrets/SecretsProtected flags, KDF metadata), Profiles.json (the full config snapshot), and either secrets.json (raw secret-store shape, unp

rotected) or secrets.protected.json (per-secret AES-256-GCM sealed blobs, password-protected).

Backup password protection exists because live secret blobs are DPAPI-sealed with DataProtectionScope.CurrentUser, binding them to one Windows user on one machine; with a password, Export decrypts each blob via the local protector and re-seals it with a PBKDF2-SHA256 (210,000 iterations, random 16-byte salt) derived AES-256-GCM key, and Import unseals and re-seals with the target machine's protector, making the backup portable. Only ciphertext is protected — Label/Account stay plaintext like the live store.

Backup import is replace-all for Profiles.json (via ConfigService.SaveAsync with no revision guard) and touches the secret store only when the package contains secrets; the pre-import secret map is staged so a failed config commit (e.g. validation rejection) rolls the secrets back, and a wrong password or tampered ciphertext surfaces as WrongPassword/InvalidSecrets without changing any target state.

Backup import validates defensively before writing anything: missing manifest.json fails as InvalidPackage, a FormatVersion newer than the supported one fails as UnsupportedVersion, unparseable Profiles.json fails as InvalidConfig, and a malformed secrets entry fails as InvalidSecrets; packages without secrets leave the current secret store untouched.

HotkeyService subscribes to IConfigService.ConfigUpdated and rebuilds its effective hotkey cache from the fresh state, keeping it in sync with every commit path (Settings save, ConfigEditSession, tutorial); ApplyHotkey intentionally mutates only the in-memory cache, never the shared snapshot, leaving persistence to the editor commit path (ADR-005).

SettingsEditorSession is the Settings window's persistence seam: it owns the ConfigEditSession lifecycle (begin/lazy-begin/commit), the working draft, and the secret-store pipeline, and its CommitAsync saves the merged secret store (secrets.json) before committing the config draft, so the editor commits config and secrets as one logical save.

The concurrency and persistence contracts are covered by focused test suites: ConfigEditSessionTests (draft isolation, stale-commit rebase-and-retry preserving both regions, ensure operations never clobber, unchanged-draft skip), ConfigServiceConcurrencyTests (injected path, 12 concurrent writers leave no temp files, reentrant ConfigUpdated save without deadlock), ConfigServiceLoadTests (backup restoration, reset semantics, migration), and ConfigBackupServiceTests (package layout, cross-protector restore, wrong-password no-op, side-effect-free failures).
